meta.source: Cole, G.M. and Mueller, T.J., 'Experimental Measurements of the Laminar Separation Bubble on an Eppler 387 Airfoil at Low Reynolds Numbers', University of Notre Dame, Final Report UNDAS-1419-FR, January 1990. Prepared under NASA Contract NSG 1419 for NASA Langley Research Center.
meta.document_type: raster scan (sparse OCR text layer); the station data below were read VISUALLY from a 300 dpi PyMuPDF render of the page
meta.important_correction: The item titled 'Summary of Laminar Separation, Transition, and Turbulent Reattachment Locations for Various Angles of Attack for the E387 Airfoil at Rc = 100,000' is NOT a numeric table in this report: it is Figure 4.37, a scatter plot (alpha vs x/c percent chord), on printed page 90 (PDF page index 102). Companion figures 4.38/4.39 (printed pages 91/92) give Re=200,000 and 300,000. The report's actual Table 4.1 'Separation Bubble Parameters' (printed page 44, PDF index 56) contains exact LDV-derived values for a single E387 case (alpha=2.0 deg) and is transcribed separately below.

figure_4_37.measurement_technique: Station locations in Fig. 4.37 were determined from the measured static pressure distributions (Figs. 4.8-4.36): laminar separation from the start of the constant-pressure plateau, transition from the plateau end / start of rapid pressure recovery, reattachment from the end of the recovery. Document states an uncertainty of +/-1% x/c. At alpha=2 they compare well with fluorescent-surface-oil flow visualization (separation 40% x/c, reattachment 80% x/c) and with LDV (Table 4.1: 39.5/76/80.5 % x/c).
figure_4_37.text_check: Report text (printed p.23) states for Re=100,000, alpha=2.0: 'laminar separation occurs at 40% x/c, transition at 76% x/c, and reattachment at 85% x/c' - this matches the digitized alpha=2 row exactly.
figure_4_37.digitization: Points read visually from zoomed crops of the 300 dpi render, calibrated against axis tick labels; readable to about +/-1 percent chord, comparable to the document's own +/-1% x/c uncertainty.
figure_4_37.units: raw values are percent chord as plotted; x/c values are the same divided by 100
ambiguities: alpha=10 laminar-separation circle sits essentially on the x/c=0 axis (short leading-edge bubble); recorded as 0.5 +/- 1 %chord.
alpha=0 separation (44%) reads slightly ahead of alpha=1 separation (46%); this non-monotonic scatter is in the plot itself.
Symbols at plot-frame edges (alpha=-2 circle at 50%, alpha=-2 triangle at 90%, alpha=10 circle at 0%) appear solid/filled, most likely because they overlap the axis/frame lines.

Between alpha=8 and alpha=9 the bubble jumps from mid-chord (~28-52%) to the leading edge (~2-10%), consistent with the report text about the rapid forward movement at alpha of seven-to-eight degrees and short LE bubble formation.

meta.tunnel_turbulence: Notre Dame south low-speed low-turbulence wind tunnel (F.N.M. Brown design): open-circuit indraft, 0.61 m x 0.61 m test section, 24:1 contraction preceded by twelve anti-turbulence screens. The report does NOT state a numeric freestream turbulence intensity; it says tests required 'as low a turbulence intensity as possible' and refers to O'Meara (1985) for measured effects of freestream turbulence on the bubble.

figure_4_38.digitization: Points read visually from zoomed crops of a 300 dpi PyMuPDF render (page rotated 90 deg to upright), calibrated against axis tick labels; readable to about +/-1 percent chord, comparable to the document's own +/-1% x/c uncertainty.
figure_4_38.attached_transition_note: Report text (printed p.24): 'The locations of attached transition were taken from Eppler's program results (Eppler, 1986).' The transition-only points at alpha=7 (32%) and alpha=8 (12%) are attached transition (no separation bubble): pressure distributions Figs 4.25-4.27 show attached transition at alpha=7,8,9 for Re=200,000.
ambiguities: alpha=7 and alpha=8 rows have a transition symbol only (attached transition from Eppler's program); no laminar-separation or reattachment symbols are plotted there. The dashed separation and reattachment curves converge toward the alpha=7 transition point.
Report text mentions attached transition at alpha=9 as well (Fig 4.27), but Figure 4.38 plots no alpha=9 symbol; the transition curve simply ends just above alpha=8.
alpha=0 has only a laminar-separation circle (48%); no transition or reattachment symbols are plotted at alpha=0, although the faired curves pass through that alpha.
alpha=-1 and alpha=-2 separation circles nearly coincide at ~54% chord (read 53.5-54.1%); both recorded as 54.
Symbols on the alpha=-2 axis line (circle 54%, triangle 82%, diamond 88%) overlap the plot frame and appear partly filled.

figure_4_39.digitization: Points read visually from zoomed crops of a 300 dpi PyMuPDF render (page rotated 90 deg to upright), calibrated against axis tick labels; readable to about +/-1 percent chord, comparable to the document's own +/-1% x/c uncertainty.
figure_4_39.attached_transition_note: Transition-only points at alpha=7 (40%), alpha=8 (20%), alpha=9 (5%) are attached-transition locations from Eppler's program (Eppler, 1986). Report text cites attached transition at alpha=7,8 (Figs 4.34-4.35) for Re=300,000 and a short leading-edge bubble at alpha=10 (Fig 4.36).
ambiguities: alpha=7,8,9 rows have transition symbols only (attached transition); dashed separation/reattachment curves converge toward the alpha=7 transition point at 40%.

The topmost triangle reads alpha=9.0 at 5% chord, but the text discusses attached transition only at alpha=7,8 and a short LE bubble at alpha=10; the alpha=9 point is presumably Eppler-program attached transition. Figure 4.39 plots nothing at alpha=10.
No alpha=-1 row exists in this figure (unlike Figs 4.37/4.38); measured-bubble alphas are -2, 0, 1, 3 only.
Symbols on the alpha=-2 axis line (circle 62%, triangle 76%, diamond 82%) overlap the plot frame; the triangle appears filled.
The alpha=3 reattachment diamond at 64% is crossed by the faired curve and appears partly filled.
